takeaways: Market concentration in AI-linked firms now drives 85% of S&P 500 gains, yet earnings quality is increasingly questioned as headline growth relies heavily on volatile, unrealized private equity gains.

Central bank credibility is under pressure as bond market skepticism and sticky global inflation suggest a prolonged 'higher for longer' rate environment, complicating the path for growth-sensitive assets.

Systemic risks are mounting as infrastructure bottlenecks, regulatory grid audits, and potential bans on Chinese hardware threaten to inflate costs and delay the massive capital expenditure fueling the AI boom.

items.title: All eyes on RBI as MPC meets amid rising inflation and global uncertainty
bullets: The Reserve Bank of India is expected to maintain its repo rate at 5.25 percent, despite retail inflation climbing to 4.38 percent in June, which marks the first breach of the 4 percent target in 17 months.
Rising food and fuel costs, compounded by geopolitical tensions in West Asia, are pressuring the central bank to adopt a more hawkish tone to ensure price stability and support the rupee.
items.reason: Significant central bank policy decision impacting emerging market currency stability.

items.title: Bond sell-off sent warning on Federal Reserve’s credibility, says top central bank official
bullets: A recent bond market sell-off has been interpreted by senior central bank officials as a direct signal of market skepticism regarding the Federal Reserve's commitment to its inflation-fighting mandate.

This loss of credibility suggests that investors are pricing in higher long-term risks, potentially forcing the Fed to maintain restrictive policy longer than previously anticipated to anchor expectations.
items.reason: Direct impact on global interest rate expectations and market sentiment.

items.title: Persistently high inflation to nag global economy, say economists: Reuters poll
bullets: Economists surveyed by Reuters indicate that global inflation is likely to remain sticky, complicating the path for central banks attempting to balance growth with price stability.
The persistence of these inflationary pressures suggests that the era of 'higher for longer' interest rates may extend further into 2026, impacting corporate earnings and consumer spending power.
items.reason: Broad macroeconomic outlook affecting global asset valuations.

items.title: S&P 500 set for first record high in two months
bullets: The S&P 500 is approaching a new closing record high, driven by a rotation into diverse sectors and a rebound in tech stocks following a two-month period of heightened volatility and AI-related anxiety.

Market sentiment received a significant boost from Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s comments regarding potential progress in negotiations to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which helped ease energy price concerns.
items.reason: Broad market index hitting record highs is a primary indicator of investor sentiment and macroeconomic health.

items.title: Why Palantir stock is ripping higher after earnings: AlphaSpace stat of the morning
bullets: Palantir shares surged 14% following a strong second quarter, characterized by a 149% year-over-year revenue growth in its US Commercial segment and a record $2.1 billion in total contract value.
Management raised full-year revenue guidance to approximately $8.15 billion, an 82% increase over the prior year, as the company benefits from parabolic demand for its AI-driven software solutions.
items.reason: Significant earnings beat and guidance raise from a bellwether AI stock impacts broader tech sector valuations.

items.title: U.S. yen intervention signals perfect storm rising in FX and bond markets
bullets: The recent joint U.S.-Japan currency intervention, aimed at stabilizing the yen near 40-year lows, highlights growing systemic risks as Japan holds US$1.14-trillion in U.S. Treasuries.

Market volatility in Japanese Government Bonds (JGBs) threatens to spill over into the U.S. Treasury market, potentially exacerbating yield spikes at a time when Fed credibility is under intense scrutiny.
items.reason: Systemic risk from major creditor instability

items.title: Fitch Says: AI Market Correction Could Be a Big Risk to Corporate Credit. That Might Be Bad News for This Junk Bond ETF.
bullets: AI-related corporate debt issuance is projected to reach nearly $570 billion in 2026, with Fitch Ratings noting that this capital expenditure contributed 1.4% to U.S. GDP growth in Q1.

A potential re-evaluation of AI's long-term profitability could trigger a credit market downturn, disproportionately impacting high-yield corporate bond ETFs that hold lower-rated, more vulnerable issuers.
items.reason: Credit risk concentration in AI-related debt

items.title: How likely is Beijing to walk the talk on boosting consumption?
bullets: China's second-quarter GDP growth slowed to 4.3%, dragging the first-half average to 4.7% and leaving the economy barely within the official 4.5-5% annual target range.

The growth deceleration is driven by a sharp 18% contraction in property investment and a significant cooling in retail sales, which grew only 0.2% in the second quarter compared to 2.4% in the first.
items.reason: Critical data showing the failure of domestic demand and property sector drag.

items.title: More patient policy framework for China's economy
bullets: The economy is transitioning into a structural 'around 4 percent growth' era, as traditional engines like real estate and infrastructure are replaced by AI and advanced manufacturing.

Economic divergence is widening between industries and income groups, creating a disconnect where official macroeconomic indicators fail to reflect the actual financial strain experienced by households and local governments.
items.reason: Provides structural context for the long-term shift in China's growth trajectory.

items.title: HSBC resumes buyback after big profit jump in first half of 2026
bullets: HSBC reported a 27% increase in profit attributable to shareholders to US$14.6 billion for the first half of 2026, driven by growth in net interest income and higher fee-based revenue.

The bank announced a US$1 billion share buyback and a second interim dividend of US$0.10 per share, signaling confidence despite incurring US$2.4 billion in expected credit losses, including exposure to Hong Kong commercial property.
items.reason: Major capital return and strong earnings from a systemically important financial institution.

items.title: Hong Kong home sales value drops 44.6pc month-on-month in July
bullets: The 44.6% month-on-month decline in home sales value for July highlights significant volatility in the local property market, contrasting sharply with earlier periods of recovery.
This sharp contraction suggests that momentum in the residential sector is stalling, potentially impacting the balance sheets of major local developers and the broader economic outlook for Hong Kong.
items.reason: Significant indicator of cooling momentum in Hong Kong's critical property sector.

items.title: Big Tech's Anthropic and OpenAI stakes are distorting the corporate earnings picture
bullets: S&P 500 earnings growth for the recent quarter is significantly inflated by unrealized investment gains in private AI firms like OpenAI and Anthropic, which are booked as 'other income'.

Adjusting for these one-time equity gains reveals a much more muted 29% earnings growth rate, compared to the 48% headline figure, highlighting a reliance on paper wealth rather than operational software sales.
items.reason: Market-wide earnings distortion

items.title: Big tech to pay more if no deal reached with Australian media
items.source: ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation
bullets: The Australian government is raising the penalty levy for tech companies that fail to secure content deals with local news publishers from 2.25% to 2.5% of digital advertising revenue.

While the penalty rate increased, tech firms secured a concession to apply the levy only to digital ad revenue rather than total company revenue, potentially limiting the financial impact of the regulation.
items.reason: Regulatory risk for tech margins

items.title: America’s Cosmic Bet on AI - Foreign Policy
bullets: AI-related investments currently account for half of all U.S. business capital expenditure, highlighting the economy's extreme concentration in the sector. AI companies now represent over 40% of total U.S. equity market value, with that figure expected to exceed 50% following upcoming trillion-dollar-plus IPOs.

The sector's dominance is reflected in broader market performance, with AI-linked firms responsible for 85% of all S&P 500 gains in 2026. This creates a significant systemic risk, as the U.S. economy has become a highly leveraged bet on the continued growth and success of artificial intelligence.
items.reason: Highlights systemic market concentration risk

items.title: Grab Says AI Helps Company Move Items 30% Faster - PYMNTS.com
bullets: Grab reported a 22% year-over-year revenue increase to $997 million, with operating profits surging 186% to $19 million, driven by AI-enabled operational efficiencies. The company successfully utilized AI to improve delivery speeds by 30% and boost driver hourly earnings by 23% through route optimization.

The firm's successful integration of AI tools, such as the 'Mai' digital assistant for merchants, demonstrates a tangible 'payback' model for enterprise AI. This provides a clear case study for investors on how AI-driven logistics can directly expand margins and scale financial services in emerging markets.
items.reason: Demonstrates tangible AI-driven margin expansion

items.title: The 1 Number Behind Nvidia’s Chip Scarcity That Most Investors Are Missing
bullets: Nvidia management has quantified its supply constraints by disclosing $1 trillion in forward revenue visibility for its Blackwell and Rubin product cycles through 2027.

The company has backed this demand with $145 billion in total supply-related commitments, including inventory purchases and prepaids, signaling that demand continues to outpace manufacturing capacity.
items.reason: Quantifies critical supply-demand dynamics for the sector leader.

items.title: SK Hynix — Not Nvidia — Has Become the Most Important AI Chip Stock on the Planet
bullets: The AI hardware bottleneck has shifted from GPU design to high-bandwidth memory (HBM) availability, making SK Hynix a critical focal point for the industry's supply chain.
Leveraged and inverse ETFs tied to SK Hynix now hold approximately $5.5 billion in assets, surpassing the total for Nvidia and signaling a major shift in speculative capital flows.
items.reason: Identifies a critical supply chain bottleneck and shifting investor sentiment.

items.title: Leapmotor Tops 100,000 Monthly Deliveries for the First Time
bullets: Leapmotor achieved a significant milestone by delivering 101,267 vehicles in July 2026, marking a 102% year-over-year increase and the first time the startup has surpassed the 100,000-unit monthly threshold.

Despite this record performance, the company must maintain a monthly delivery average of approximately 108,449 vehicles over the final five months of 2026 to reach its ambitious 1 million unit annual target.
items.reason: Significant growth milestone for a major Chinese EV player with global expansion implications.

items.title: EV sales outpace ZEV Mandate trajectory again as groups warn against policy changes
bullets: UK battery electric vehicle (BEV) registrations rose by nearly 50% in July compared to the previous year, capturing 27.4% of the market and consistently outperforming the government's ZEV mandate trajectory.

While BEV sales remain robust, the broader UK automotive sector faces headwinds, with total vehicle production falling 7.5% in the first half of 2026, prompting industry calls for urgent industrial strategy reform.
items.reason: Highlights critical regulatory and production dynamics in a major European automotive market.

items.title: Texas governor directs PUCT, ERCOT to audit all data centers seeking grid connection
bullets: Governor Greg Abbott has mandated a comprehensive audit of all data center projects in the ERCOT interconnection queue, effectively halting progress on new grid connections until compliance with state law is verified.

The directive forces a postponement of the 'Batch Zero' transmission planning study, signaling a major regulatory shift where developers must now prove financial viability and physical executability before securing grid access.
items.reason: Significant regulatory bottleneck in a primary AI infrastructure growth market.

items.title: EXCLUSIVE: Trump administration drafting ban on Chinese data center devices, sources say
bullets: The administration is reportedly drafting a ban on the use of Chinese-manufactured devices within U.S. data centers, a move that could force a massive, costly supply chain overhaul for hyperscalers and enterprise operators.

This potential policy escalation targets critical infrastructure security and follows broader efforts to decouple the U.S. AI ecosystem from Chinese hardware, likely impacting procurement costs and project timelines for data center builds.
items.reason: Major geopolitical risk with direct implications for hardware supply chains and capital expenditure.

items.title: Rocket Lab’s $8 Billion Iridium Acquisition Creates a Powerful, Profitable Space Stock in 2027
bullets: Rocket Lab is pivoting from a pure-play launch provider to a vertically integrated space business by acquiring Iridium Communications for $8 billion, aiming to capture high-margin recurring revenue from satellite data and connectivity services.

Financial projections indicate the company will narrow its annual losses to approximately $24 million in 2027 while achieving positive free cash flow for the first time as its launch and manufacturing segments mature.
items.reason: Major M&A activity signaling a shift in business model and path to profitability.

items.title: Musk likely to face tough questions during SpaceX's first earnings call as a public company
bullets: SpaceX faces significant investor scrutiny as it reports its first quarterly earnings, with shares currently trading at roughly half their June peak amid concerns over aggressive growth projections and high cash burn.

The company is entering a volatile period as lockup provisions expire, releasing over 800 million shares for trading, which will more than double the current public float and likely pressure share prices in the near term.
items.reason: First public earnings report and major share unlock event for a high-profile stock.
